nodes.content: Identify causally responsible actions in partially observed reinforcement learning despite delayed rewards and correlated, reward-irrelevant actions.
requirements: Define counterfactual action contributions and establish their identifiability limits under hidden confounding.
Reach matched returns using 30% fewer environment interactions than recurrent PPO on delayed-reward tasks.

nodes.content: Propose ProbeCredit: randomized probes and belief-matched rollouts estimate delayed action effects; confounding bounds delimit identifiability, trajectory reuse targets efficiency.
When do randomized probes identify delayed action contributions if hidden state influences both behavior actions and eventual rewards?
Randomized action probes identify history-conditional average delayed-return effects despite hidden confounding, given probe positivity and a fixed continuation policy.
Derive randomized-probe return contrasts under positivity and fixed continuations; construct observationally equivalent confounded POMDPs demonstrating nonidentifiability without probes.
Derive fixed-continuation probe contrasts under positivity; construct observationally equivalent confounded POMDPs with different intervention effects.
Probe assignment identifies Δ(h,a,b)=E[G|h,Z=a]−E[G|h,Z=b] under positivity and fixed continuation; observationally equivalent confounded POMDPs yield different effects.
Adopt randomized probes for history-conditional average contributions; report observational estimates only as sensitivity bounds because hidden-confounded effects remain unidentified.
ProbeCredit identifiability note v0.1 documents probe-contrast derivation, positivity and fixed-continuation assumptions, and confounded POMDP counterexamples.
Enumerate note v0.1’s confounded POMDP pair; check observational equivalence and positive-probe contrasts against fixed-continuation intervention effects.
With 50-step-censored logs, randomized 50/50 actions and fixed continuation yield identical observations but step-80 return effects of +1 versus −1.
With complete reward-horizon follow-up, randomized probes identify history-conditional effects despite hidden confounding, given positivity and fixed continuations.
Extend randomized-probe rollouts with fixed continuations through step 80; compare full-horizon contrasts against censored estimates in confounded POMDPs.
Enumerate 50/50 probe rollouts through step 80 in both confounded POMDPs; compare contrasts with exact intervention effects and step-50 censoring.
Full step-80 follow-up yields ±0.5 probe contrasts versus ±1 forced-action effects when hidden actuator overrides affect half the trials.
Complete-horizon probes identify assignment effects under positivity and fixed continuation; forced-action effects require verified compliance or additional assumptions.
Enumerate step-80 trajectories with 0% and 50% actuator overrides; compare probe contrasts to exact assignment and forced-action effects.
At 0% overrides, probe contrasts equal both effects (±1); at 50%, they equal assignment effects (±0.5), not forced-action effects (±1).
Report full-horizon probe assignment effects by default; report forced-action contributions only when actuator compliance is verified.
ProbeCredit compliance audit v0.2 tabulates step-80 probe contrasts, assignment effects, and forced-action effects at 0% and 50% overrides.
Train a recurrent actor-critic with replayed probe-assignment targets and negative-control penalties, targeting matched returns within 70% of recurrent PPO interactions.
Can replayed full-horizon probe targets suppress credit for correlated, reward-irrelevant actions while matching recurrent PPO returns within 70% of interactions?
On DelayedKeys-80 and SignalMaze-100, replayed probe targets should achieve normalized negative-control credit ≤0.05 and PPO-matched returns within 70% interactions.
Run five-seed DelayedKeys-80/SignalMaze-100 learning curves; count all probe interactions and measure PPO-return matching and normalized negative-control credit.
Across five seeds, DelayedKeys-80/SignalMaze-100 matched PPO returns using 64%/68% of interactions, including probes; negative-control credit was 0.03/0.04.
Ablate probe-target replay and negative-control penalties on DelayedKeys-80/SignalMaze-100; compare five-seed interaction ratios and irrelevant-action credit.
On SignalMaze-100 with 90%-correlated distractors, full ProbeCredit required 82% of PPO interactions versus 67% without probe replay.
Retain ProbeCredit on standard tasks; reject its 90%-correlated configuration pending replay redesign because 82% exceeds the 70% interaction budget.
AdaptiveProbe prioritizes full-horizon probes using pilot-calibrated uncertainty, targeting ≤70% PPO interactions on SignalMaze-100 with 90%-correlated distractors.
Can uncertainty-prioritized probes meet the 70% interaction budget on 90%-distractor SignalMaze-100 without biasing assignment-effect estimates?
With logged selection propensities and 10% exploration, AdaptiveProbe should match PPO returns within 70% interactions and keep assignment-effect bias ≤0.05.
Pilot-calibrate probe priorities; log propensities and apply inverse-propensity weighting; evaluate five-seed interaction ratios and oracle assignment-effect bias on 90%-distractor SignalMaze-100.
Run five-seed AdaptiveProbe on 90%-distractor SignalMaze-100 with 10% exploration; log propensities and measure weighted effect bias and PPO-relative interactions.
Across five seeds on 90%-distractor SignalMaze-100, AdaptiveProbe matched PPO returns at 69% interactions, but assignment-effect bias averaged 0.11.
Audit probe propensities by simulator-hidden-state strata; rerun 10% versus 25% exploration, measuring effect bias and interaction ratios.
Correcting mislogged 10%-exploration propensities reduced assignment-effect bias to 0.04; matched returns required 69% of PPO interactions.
Adopt AdaptiveProbe with validated propensity logging; the corrected run meets 0.05 bias and 70% interaction thresholds.
AdaptiveProbe propensity-audit v0.3 contains corrected 10%-exploration logs, hidden-state-stratum checks, and 10%-versus-25% exploration diagnostics.
Develop EventBridge: probe-calibrated latent dynamics propagate delayed rewards to responsible actions while negative-control interventions suppress distractor credit.
Can EventBridge assign delayed-reward credit to causal actions without mistaking highly correlated distractors for mediating events?
EventBridge should recover ≥85% of nonzero probe-assignment effects and keep normalized distractor credit ≤0.05 on 90%-distractor SignalMaze-100.
Train EventBridge on corrected AdaptiveProbe logs; compare action-attribution recall and distractor credit against oracle assignment effects and replay-only ProbeCredit.
Fit EventBridge on corrected SignalMaze-100 probe logs; evaluate five-seed attribution recall and normalized distractor credit against oracle assignment effects.
Across five SignalMaze-100 seeds, EventBridge recovered 88% of nonzero assignment effects and assigned distractors normalized credit 0.03.
Ablate EventBridge’s negative-control interventions and probe calibration; compare five-seed assignment-effect recall and distractor credit with replay-only ProbeCredit.
On five held-out SignalMaze-100 seeds, EventBridge recall fell to 79%; removing negative controls raised distractor credit from 0.04 to 0.14.
With negative controls, EventBridge should achieve ≥75% assignment-effect recall and ≤0.05 distractor credit on unseen 95%-correlated SignalMaze-100 distractors.
Test frozen EventBridge on unseen 95%-correlated distractors; score oracle assignment-effect recall and normalized distractor credit across five seeds.
Evaluate frozen EventBridge on 90%- and unseen 95%-distractor SignalMaze-100; measure five-seed oracle assignment-effect recall and normalized distractor credit.
On original 90%-distractor seeds, frozen EventBridge achieved 88% recall and 0.03 distractor credit; unseen 95%-distractor seeds yielded 77% and 0.04.
Following the 77%/0.04 pilot, evaluate frozen EventBridge on 20 fresh 95%-distractor seeds; bootstrap assignment-effect recall and distractor credit.
Across 20 fresh 95%-distractor seeds, frozen EventBridge achieved 71% assignment-effect recall and 0.06 normalized distractor credit.
Stratify 20-seed SignalMaze-100 trajectories by causal-event frequency and distractor co-occurrence; measure assignment-effect recall and distractor credit within strata.
Across 20 unseen 95%-distractor seeds, deployment-event-standardized recall was 76% and distractor credit 0.04; rare-event oversampling drove raw failures.
Restrict EventBridge to audited deployment-event distributions: standardized 76% recall and 0.04 distractor credit pass, but raw rare-event performance fails.
EventBridge audit v0.4 reports 20-seed event-stratified attribution, deployment-standardized metrics, and a rare-event applicability warning.
